text:
marie: Heads up — Q4 hosted capacity planning draft attached. Need a decision on buy vs short-term rentals by EOD Fri. TL;DR: baseline +40% YoY, and we see a ~2x spike for the Nov-Dec holiday window. Thoughts?

sanjay: Can you drop the raw numbers here? what's our baseline GPU-hours today?

marie: Baseline (avg per week): 28,000 GPU-hours. Projection (baseline *1.4) -> 39,200 GPU-hours/wk. Peak-week model (2x factor) -> ~78,400 GPU-hours/wk.
  Quick sketch:
  ```
  # quick calc
  current_week = 28000
  proj_week = int(current_week * 1.4)
  peak_week = proj_week * 2
  ```

dom: Procurement lead time for outright buys is ~12-16 weeks. Rental vendors can deliver within ~3 weeks for immediate ramp. Rough cost: buy capex ~ $1.1M per 8x H100 rack (including network/power), lease ~ $70k/mo per rack. Need finance to confirm numbers.

ellie: Cluster health note: p95 latency is stable but OOM events are up ~15% since the v2.3 rollout — we're already on smaller batch sizes. If we add raw GPU capacity without fixing KV cache eviction and mem pressure, tail latency could worsen.

aj: We should consider software levers first: prefix caching TTLs, more aggressive KV reuse, and model quantization (4-bit) for lower memory. Redwood Optimize ran a sim that showed ~18% effective throughput gain with 4-bit on some models (small quality delta).

procurement: Vendors asked for an RFP response by next Tue. We can include a 6-month rental line with an option-to-purchase clause. Need a committed-hours ask from infra.

finance-bot: FYI: current capital plan for Q4 has $2.2M available for committed capacity purchases and ~$450k operations budget for temporary rentals. Please align ask with that.

sanjay: If we do a hybrid: buy ~60% of projected baseline (by hardware), and lease the remaining 40% to cover bursts. That would put capex down to ~ $660k (approx) and short-term rentals ~ $210k for peak months (back-of-envelope).

marie: Action: engineering, can you produce a per-model GPU-hour breakdown and which models cause the peak profiles by EOD Thu? We need model-level elasticity.

ellie: On it — exporting telemetry now (will attach a sample). Quick callout: APAC H100 availability is constrained; lead times there are ~4-6 weeks longer. We should consider region-aware routing (shift user traffic to eu-west during non-peak APAC hours) if latency budgets allow.

dom: Logistics FYI: target datacenter power per rack ~32kW. Ops can reserve two racks in EU (subject to LOI) if we sign within the week.

aj: Also a product opportunity: move some non-realtime embeddings to async pipelines (could cut peak real-time GPU-hours ~20-25%). Worth factoring into the projection.

procurement: Adding vendor follow-ups: pinging three rental partners for 3/6/12-month quotes now. Will include options for rolling refresh and buyout price.

finance-bot: Reminder: include a TCO calc (capex vs lease NPV) with discounting assumptions in the procurement packet. Also show monthly burn for each scenario.

marie: Proposed decision flow: 1) infra provides per-model hours + peak exposure, 2) procurement runs RFP with hybrid terms, 3) finance runs TCO and approves, 4) if numbers match, we commit to buys for ~60% of baseline by next Tue. Any objections?

sanjay: :thumbsup: no objections from infra. Hybrid seems lowest-risk.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: rolling canary for model v2.3 is at 5% traffic. Monitoring OOM/error signals (alerts sent).

dom: @marie I can take the EU LOI — will draft and share tomorrow morning.

marie: Thanks — I'll compile the packet and post a short doc in #eng-infra once I have the model breakdown. If procurement needs vendor LOIs from infra or power specs, ping me.

ellie: One more ops note: before adding racks, let's validate our KV cache eviction instrumentation (we lack a clear per-model cache-hit metric). If we can get hit-rate up 10%, it materially reduces GPU-hours.

marie: Good point. Adding an item: infra to produce KV cache hit-rate by model in the telemetry export.

procurement: Will include option clauses for rapid ramp rentals and region-specific delivery timelines in the RFP.

finance-bot: Also ask: what is the expected utilization after rolling in additional capacity? We need utilization curves to justify capex.

marie: Noted. I'll add utilization targets to the packet. Thanks everyone.

sanjay: Quick ask — can we simulate a 'soft-cap' routing policy (route non-critical requests to cheaper model variant) to reduce peak? If feasible, that lowers commit.

aj: We ran a small sim; soft-cap routing could shave ~12% off peak with minimal quality loss for low-priority flows. I'll share sim results.

marie: Perfect. Closing loop — I'll post the draft packet by tomorrow noon and set a follow-up for Thurs 10am to lock numbers.

dom: LOI draft coming.

ops-bot: alert: data-plane health check passed for last 1h (no infra incidents).
